newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet decides to free fuel prices - PAP.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet decides to free fuel prices - PAP.

text.p: The Polish government decided on Tuesday on the timetable for freeing fuel prices, PAP news agency quoted an anonymous senior government official as saying.

Fuel prices in Poland are controlled by the finance ministry which has long been reluctant to let them rise, despite a jump in world oil prices, out of fear that this would cause a strong inflationary impulse.

"It is one of the last moments to do this (free prices) because of business cycles. Later it will be impossible," PAP late on Tuesday quoted the official as saying. The official did not give any specific date for the freeing of prices.

Government caps on domestic fuel prices have seriously cut the profits of Poland's refineries, which have had to buy crude oil at world prices and sell their products at the maximum prices set by the ministry.

The freeing of fuel prices is the key to the restructuring of Poland's oil sector which will lead to the privatisation of refineries. The issue was not on the government's agenda for its Tuesday session.
Neither the government's press office nor the finance ministry or industry officials would immediately confirm or deny the report.
Under a 1996 agreement with the European Union Poland promised to free fuel prices in exchange for extended protection of its domestic fuel market.
